CLIMATE ACTION 
Climate Action Plan (CAP) 
1. Progression of feasibility study for District Heating in Carrick-on-Shannon with consultant AECOM 
Ireland is ongoing.  Stakeholder engagement frozen, model of preferred locations / heat source.  
Final report expected, April 2026 
2. Met Jacinta Barrins with Community Development (10 February 2026) about roll out of an 11-week 
course for Over-55s (Sept – Dec ‘26) along with Sligo and Donegal LAs. 
3. DCEE Webinar on Horizon funding (11 February ‘26), open to end of 2027.  A new fund of €1.5m in 
2026 for climate action across all local authorities (detail TBC) 
4. Support for Fair Trade month in Carrick-on-Shannon, launch (4 February 2026) and parade (24 
February 26) 
5. Met LDC on seed library (11 February ‘26), Library to facilitate subject to appropriate protocol.  To 
meet Kildare CC on their experience.  Caillin Reynolds (LDC) presented on Leitrim Community 
Garden Network, CA lunch and learn (27 February ‘26). 
6. Carrick-on-Shannon Climate Action DZ taskforce meeting (24 February ‘26), minutes available 
7. Discussion and preparation of potential projects within the Decarbonising Zone for funding 
application(s) to NWRA ERDF DZ Scheme under Climate Adaptation and Green Infrastructure 
themes.  Potential for €50k for Project type 1 (plans / studies) or €250k (shovel ready 
implementation).  Deadline moved to 6 March 2026 
8. Support Arts on lead for application to Creative Climate fund, open until 15 April 2026.  Shared Island 
element, requirement for partnerships.  Potential €400,000 - €750,000 available

COMMUNITY AND INTERGATION 
Local Enhancement Programme 2026 
Applications for LEP 2026 closed on the 27th February, with 177 applications received. Leitrim’s 
allocation for 2026 is €119,043.40.  
Age Friendly Programme   
Leitrim’s Age Friendly Programme Manager, Technical Advisor and Healthy Age Friendly Homes 
Coordinator attended the Age Friendly Ireland National Residential Meeting. This was the first time all 
Age Friendly job roles attended a residential meeting together and the event provided an opportunity for 
enhanced networking and learning. 
The National Older People's Convention takes place in Athlone in 2026 with rooms reserved for Leitrim’s 
representatives.  
 
Healthy Ireland 
The 2025 report for Healthy Ireland has now been completed and submitted to Pobal. All expressions of 
interest have been circulated to implementing partners for 2026 and budget has been agreed.  Service 
level agreements are being signed and all programme funding will be allocated to implementing 
partners by March 13th. The period dignity report has been submitted to the Department of Health and 
funding for 2026 has been applied for.

4 
 
Community Recognition Fund 
Leitrim has been allocated over €2.2 million under this funding programme, which is being 16 capital 
projects throughout the county. As at the end of January 2026, 6 of these projects have been completed.  
Love Where You Live 
The Love Where You Live Primary Schools competition is now open for all Primary Schools in Leitrim to 
enter part by submitting a project inspired by this year’s theme, Climate Action. The deadline for 
submissions is Friday, 24th April 2026. 
Leitrim PEACEPLUS Action Plan (1.1) 
Local Community Regeneration & Transformation 
• Play & Art Therapy Centre, Drumkeeran - Contractor Paul Gallagher formally appointed and works 
have commenced onsite. 
• Construction works proceeding on schedule at  Coleman’s (Carrick Youth Arts & Community Space) 
• Maguire Architects have been appointed to Project Manage MUGA in Ballinamore. Tender package 
currently being prepared. 
Thriving & Peaceful Communities  
• QQI Level 7 - 25 progressing with programme. Two online session & a 2-day residential on NUI 
Maynooth Campus have been completed to date 
• Volunteer Support Programme - Tender awarded to Leitrim Volunteer Centre, contract signed & 
project initiation meeting held 16.02.26. Will be working with Joe Mooney Summer School on Youth 
Volunteer element -  4 weeks of summer camps in The junction & Dromahair Court House 
• Digital Camps for Young People - Feb Mid-Term - Kinlough - 3 days delivered by the Fab lab 12 & 
13th Feb. 2 days in The Junction with Foróige Youth Scape Group & Youth Reach                           
• 24.02.25 - YSI Scratch Trip to DCU with 20 students from Mohill CS 
Celebrating Cultural Diversity  
• Practical Skills Training Programme - Ballinamore Area Community Council to roll out training 
opportunities in tractor skills, ATV (quad bike), LANTRA-F – Bespoke agricultural First Aid, Safe Pass 
Certification, Abrasive Wheel & Safety Awareness/Physical Awareness. 
• Diversity Through the Arts – Planning 1 week summer camp in 2026 for drama project with young 
people with Downs Syndrome & their parents/guardians 
• Technical Training Camps for Young People - 30 Mar – 3 April – Film Camp planned for The Junction, 
Ballinamore.  
PEACEPLUS Shannonside Peace Arena (1.4) 
• The second Project Board meeting of 2026 was held in February, with representation from SEUPB, 
the Department for Communities (NI), DRCDG, McAdam Design, and SRC. 
• The Large-Scale Infrastructure Fund (LSSIF) application has entered its final review stage ahead of 
resubmission, incorporating updated financial projections and business costings, with submission 
targeted for the end of the month.  
• LCC's PEACEPLUS Co-ordinator and Development Officer met with a representative of the SRC 
Accounts Committee to refine and streamline reporting processes and timelines. 
• McAdam Design supplied LCC with the project's environmental compliance requirements through 
a BREEAM checklist, which is currently being progressed.  
• LCC released an updated project timeline video and accompanying press release across council 
websites, local media, and social media platforms to showcase progress on the SRC project and 
outline forthcoming milestones.

Management 
• Crowleys DFK auditors have been working on certifying our claims. Under the Council Action Plan 
we have 6 Claims up on the Jems Portal from Oct 2023 to June 2025. Claim periods are quarterly 
and our first 2 claims have been certified with no deductions.  
➢ Claim 1 - €24,176.94 
➢ Claim 2 - €30,411.42 
➢ We have responded to detailed queries on Claims 3, 4 & 5 are awaiting certification on these. 
• The Shannonside Peace Arena Letter of Offer dates from Nov 2024 and there are 3 Claims on the 
portal.  LCC have zero expenditure for first 2 claim periods and Claim 3, amounting to €19, 553.61 
is currently under verification by Crowleys. 
Local Community Safety Partnership (LCSP) 
• Inaugural Meeting for Leitrim LCSP held. Pat Forde elected as Chairperson, Cllr Maeve Reynolds 
elected as Vice Chair.  
• Attendance at National Office of Community Safety Network Meeting 
• Meeting held of Youth Drug and Alcohol Education Awareness Working Group, Consultation Survey 
with Post Primary School Principals/Coordinator around the County commended to establish 
status of education delivery to young people at present  
• Development of Community & Integration Operating Procedure for Humanitarian Response 
developed, training programme for Emergency Helpline being developed.  
• 8 Primary CSC’s now have generator switches installed and testing carried out in each MD by Civil 
Defence and Facilities 
• Funding recoupment from Dept has commenced for both Generators and Switch installations 
• 11 satellite CSC’s identified with EOI, inspection and quotation process ongoing.   
Local Authority Integration Team (LAIT) 
In February, the IRPP Working Group held its first meeting. The Integration Team delivered nine clinics to 
assess needs and connect participants with appropriate supports—two for Beneficiaries of Temporary 
Protection (BOTP) and seven in IPAS Centres. A consultation evening was also held in an IPAS Centre to 
gather resident feedback and promote community engagement. 
Additionally, two information sessions took place: 
• 
Community Volunteering Session - Open to all community members, highlighting the value of 
volunteering and attended by both BOTP and IPA participants. 
• 
Housing Information Session for IPAs - Delivered by DePaul, covering documentation 
requirements, social housing and HAP applications, and preparation for entering the private rental 
market. 
There were no activations for Offer a Home in February.

LIBRARY SERVICES 
During the month of February, the usual events such as book club and writer group meetings as well as 
craft groups, scrabble, bridge and language sessions took place.  Creative writing for Young Adults 
continued in Dromahair Library. Women's Wellbeing Talk by Maj Cunningham was hosted in Dromahair, 
Carrick, Drumshanbo and Mohill Libraries. OurKidz Coding Workshop continued in Drumshanbo Library 
and was well received. There was good usage of the Sensory Room at Mohill Library and Cubbie at 
Manorhamilton Library.  
Ireland Reads Campaign 
Ireland Reads day took place on Saturday 28th February. The Ireland Reads Campaign which encourages 
everybody to rediscover the joy of reading and ‘to get lost in a good book’ ran throughout the month of 
February. Staff from all branch libraries in the county posted personal recommendations and 
encouraged local ambassadors to promote reading and library services via social media video clips. 
Branches held events in the lead up to the Ireland Reading Day and on the day itself. Events included - 
Author Joe Nestor facilitating an event in Carrick-on-Shannon and Dromahair library while 
Manorhamilton Library hosted an event by author Brian Leydon. 
Dementia Inclusive Club 
A new bi-weekly Dementia Inclusive Social Club has commenced in Carrick on-Shannon Library. The club 
is a social gathering where people can access information and support, meet other people and exchange 
ideas and experiences.  
Shannon Waters Flow Project 
Shannon water flows was launched at Ballinamore Library on Wednesday, February 25th at 7pm.  This 
project explores the songs, stories and cultural change of 1920s Leitrim. The project, Shannon Waters 
Flow, led by traditional singer and researcher Fionnuala Maxwell was funded by the Department of 
Culture, Communications and Sport  
A major strand of Shannon Waters Flow involves making archive material accessible to new audiences. 
Digitised audio, historical notes and curated resources are being shared through library platforms and 
the Rakes of Music collection. The launch event in Ballinamore Library featured an illustrated talk, live 
performances of songs from the period, projected archival material and a demonstration of newly 
created digital resources.

ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT 
STEM Passport for Inclusion- Maynooth University & ATU 
Engagement with employers on supporting the STEM passport for inclusion Programme with work 
placements was carried out in February 2026. 
STEMtacular 2026 
This event took place on February 25th & 26th, support in the form of staff time across the two days and 
sponsorship were given given.  
Carrick on Shannon Community CCTV Scheme Extension 
Engaged J&N Security consulting to prepare revised costings for phase 2 of the Carrick Community CCTV 
Scheme. 
Carrick on Shannon Business Campus 
Meetings with BABLE GmbH and the working group commenced in February to progress the consultancy 
services for the priming phase of the proposed Enterprise Hub at the Carrick-on-Shannon Business 
Campus. Stakeholder consultations are scheduled to take place in early March. 
Leitrim Economic Forum  
The Leitrim Economic Forum meeting took place on February 6th; a significant part of this meeting was 
dedicated to a consultation workshop with members on the the upcoming Economic and Skills Strategy. 
The next meeting of the Economic Forum will take place on May 8th, 2026. 
Global Business Network 
 A meeting of the Leitrim Global Business Network took place on 24 February 2026. Work is progressing 
on the planning for the Leitrim Ambassadors Summit, which is set to take place on 24th and 25th of 
September 2026. The Working Group are continuing to meet on a regular basis to progress matters.  
Remote Working Marketing Campaign 
The evaluation of submissions for the tender to appoint consultants for a social media marketing 
campaign was completed in February, and the successful consultant will be appointed in early March. 
DRCD Funded Schemes 
The Town and Village letter of offer has been issued by the Department and letters have now been issued 
to successful projects funded under Town and Village scheme 2025.  
Information Briefing sessions took place in the three MD’s during February in the following locations 
Drumshanbo, Manorhamilton and Mohill. The sessions covered CLÁR, Town and Village and ORIS 
funding schemes.  
The Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht, Dara Calleary TD, has announced 
the Sixth Call for Category 1 proposals for the Rural Regeneration and Development Fund (RRDF) was 
open on Friday 27th February, with a closing date of 28th July 2026

10 
TOURISM 
Marketing  
The first phase of the LEADER funded 2026 marketing campaign was successfully launched, delivering a 
broad and coordinated media presence. The campaign combined TV advertising, radio broadcasts, video 
on demand placements, and podcast advertising to ensure comprehensive audience coverage. 
Engagement was further strengthened through prize giveaways on RTÉ 2FM and RTÉ Lyric FM, helping to 
drive listener participation and brand recall. Performance data is being reviewed continuously, with early 
results indicating strong reach, high visibility, and positive engagement trends across all channels. The 
central call to action directed audiences to the website - www.enjoyleitrim.ie, where businesses from 
across the county submitted special offers designed to encourage visit and local spend. 
Presentations  
The Tourism Team delivered a presentation to the Rural Development Coordination Group outlining 
progress on current initiatives and introducing several new projects in development. The update also 
included an overview of Failte Ireland’s regional Destination Experience Development Plans highlighting 
how national priorities align with local tourism objectives and upcoming opportunities for collaboration. 
Support Initiatives 
Applications for the St. Patrick’s Day Events were received and evaluated and 12 towns and villages 
across the County have received funding support.  All events will be promoted across all the social media 
channels.  Festival and Community Grants Scheme was also live with a closing date of the 1st March.  
Meetings 
Attendance at the initial preparation meeting for the EU Presidency twinning arrangement with Cyprus 
marked the beginning of Leitrim’s involvement in the programme. As part of Ireland’s upcoming EU 
Presidency, Leitrim has been formally twinned with Cyprus for the duration of the term. The meeting 
focused on outlining the objectives of the twinning initiative, early planning requirements, and 
opportunities for tourism, cultural, civic, and community exchange between both regions. 
LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE (LEO) 
Training, Mentoring & Export      
A number of people received training in February as we ran a series of courses such as Canva for Beginners; 
How to Develop a Winning Business Plan and a Marketing Advice Clinic.  
Demand for one-to-one mentoring continues to remain high. Assistance is also available on Export related 
issues and can be booked online free of charge to discuss any issues facing businesses or identifying and 
managing opportunities available for exporting. 
All In A Days Work Programmes & Associated Financial Supports 
The “All In A Days Work” campaign continues to be rolled out on the areas of Lean, Green and Digital 
supports.  There is significant growth in demand for all three supports, in particular the Energy Efficiency 
Grant (EEG) and Grow Digital (GD) Voucher.   The EEG, with up to 75% of eligible costs up to a maximum 
grant of €10,000 can be supported following the completion of a Green for Business, Green Start or a SEAI 
Energy Audit.   The GD voucher is a grant covering 50% of eligible costs (minimum grant of €500 up to a 
maximum grant of €5,000) limited to new software subscriptions for a period of 12 and training and 
configuration of the software.

Interreg Europe Digital Rural: Leitrim continues its partnership under Interreg Europe. The Digital Rural 
Project empowers rural communities through smart technologies and collaborative policymaking to 
foster sustainable regional development.  
PEACE Plus – DS3 Project 
As part of the DS3 Project under PEACE Plus (Smart Towns & Villages) workshops and clinics with the 
Mobile Fab Lab have commenced. The project will run until July 2028 and offers free digital mentoring, 
skills development and community-focused digital inclusion activities. This programme will be of 
interest to SMEs, micro businesses, community/voluntary groups and individuals located in rural towns 
and villages.  
Creative Heartlands 
The programme ‘Creative Heartlands on Screen’ continues with training and mentoring for the screen 
sector in Leitrim, Sligo and Roscommon with funding from Screen Ireland. Training and networking 
events have commenced and will run until May 2026. A comprehensive mentorship programme is being 
established.  
Northwest Regional Enterprise Plan Implementation 
Northwest Vision Development 
The 3 Chief Executives from Leitrim/Sligo/Donegal are collaborating to develop a Northwest Region Vision 
which will feed into the REP development in 2026. Leitrim CoCo is represented on the project by Director 
of Economic Development and the NW Programme Manager.  A presentation from the consultants OCO 
was made to group in late January.  The draft document will be considered by the group in early February 
with direction given to OCO for final document.   
Energy Working Group 
A multi-agency supported project is underway which will explore the opportunities available to both the 
Northwest and West Regions with available unused energy from our renewable energy sources e.g. 
onshore wind energy. Opportunities being explored are green energy parks, marketing, hydrogen etc. 
Leitrim CoCo is represented on the project by Director of Economic Development and the NW Programme 
Manager. The West REP is taking the lead on this project with next steps include finalizing report, securing 
buy-in and hosting regional/online seminars on findings. 
10xNW 2026 
Following a very successful event in 2025, a collaborative course of multiple agencies in the Northwest 
region are coming together to host the 10xNW entrepreneurship exchange in February 2026 in Leitrim. A 
half day workshop was held in late January with 11 entrepreneurs in preparation for the two-day event in 
February.  
Next REP development 
The final report of the Northwest Regional Enterprise Plan 2022-2025 is currently in draft form and was 
submitted to DETE in mid-January.  Once approved by DETE will be published on DETE website.  
Currently DETE are undergoing a review of the REPs with the intention of taking recommendations from 
the review towards the next REP development which is due to kick off Q1 2026.

A Part 8 Public Consultation process was underway with respect to the remodelling of the existing hard-
standing plaza area to the front and side of the Dock, Carrick-on-Shannon. Submissions were invited 
before 4th February 2026. It is intended to bring a recommendation to the March Carrick-on-Shannon 
Municipal District meeting. A further Part 8 Public Consultation process is underway with respect to an 
Active Travel project consisting of junction tightening and pedestrian priority upgrades at six locations 
within Drumshanbo. Submissions are invited before 20th April 2026. 
Forward Planning 
Variation to County Development Plan 2023-2029 
We are presently at the stage of consultation on SEA scoping with designated environmental authorities 
which issued on 25th February last. We intend to publish our draft Variation on 15th April.   
Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) 
Draft RZLT maps were published on Friday 30th January and public consultation will run until April 1st. All 
of the information relating to the RZLT and the manner in which affected landowners can make 
submissions is on our website.
